lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eSilla\u003c/b\u003e:: "Chair: strain-free; 6 axial and 6 equatorial H atoms."
lit.\u0027\u003cp class=\"muted small\"\u003:
"

A-values (kcal/mol): H 0 · F 0.15 · Br 0.38 · Cl 0.43 · OH 0.87 · CH₃ 1.74 · t-Bu ≈ 4.9. ΔG° = A × 4.184 kJ/mol; K = eΔG°/RT.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAxial, el metilo choc:
"

When axial, the methyl clashes with the axial H atoms on C3 and C5 (1,3-diaxial interactions, orange lines), ≈ 7.3 kJ/mol (A = 1.74 kcal/mol). Result: at equilibrium ≈ 95 % of the molecules have the methyl equatorial (ΔG = −RT ln K).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl A-value del \u003c:
"

The A-value of tert-butyl is ≈ 4.9 kcal/mol (≈ 20 kJ/mol): the conformation with axial t-Bu practically does not exist (< 0.01 %). The ring is locked with equatorial t-Bu; it is used as a directing group in studies of stereoelectronic reactivity.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl ciclohexano adopta:
"

Cyclohexane adopts the chair conformation: free of angle strain (≈ 111°) and torsional strain (everything staggered). Each carbon has one axial substituent (parallel to the axis, in orange) and one equatorial substituent (pointing out of the ring). Axial and equatorial positions alternate up/down.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el butano (giro de:
"

In butane (rotation about the C2–C3 bond) more minima and maxima appear: anti (CH₃ at 180°, the most stable, 0), gauche (±60°, +3.8 kJ/mol due to steric strain), eclipsed CH₃/H (≈ +16 kJ/mol) and eclipsed CH₃/CH₃ (≈ +19 kJ/mol, maximum).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la \u003cb\u003epr:
"

In the Newman projection we look along the C–C bond: the front carbon is the central point and the back one is the circle. The rotational barrier of ethane is ≈ 12 kJ/mol, attributed to torsional repulsion (and to σC–H→σ*C–H hyperconjugation in the staggered form). It is crossed billions of times per second at 25 °C.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003einver:
"

The chair flip converts one chair into the other through the half-chair (≈ 45 kJ/mol), twist-boat and boat. All axial substituents become equatorial and vice versa. At 25 °C it happens ~10⁵ times per second; the barrier is ≈ 45 kJ/mol.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos enlaces σ C–C per:
"

The C–C σ bonds allow free rotation. The different spatial arrangements obtained by rotating are called conformations. In ethane, rotating one methyl relative to the other alternates between the staggered (more stable) and eclipsed (less stable) arrangements.

"
